claim: The walkthrough holds 40 PNGs on disk plus 2 not on disk (01-landing, 37-blank-step1, read as OCR). The combined text file 99-all-page-text.txt holds 41 page captures. Screenshots show only the first viewport; the text captures carry below-the-fold content that the pixels miss: the full Settings/Advanced page (conversational behaviour, alerting, privacy), the Security tab limits, the full LLM and language lists, the Architect deployment checklist and the full template list.

Some captures are not what their file name says: 02-after-login.png is the template gallery, not an agents list; 63-voice-picker.png is the 'Agent voice' settings drawer, not a list of voices; 38-agent-builder.png caught the voice row still on 'Loading'; 12-knowledge-base.png is the workspace-level KB and 7-knowledge-base.png the agent-level KB. The text captures carry hCaptcha, Stripe and Cookiebot iframe noise, and the template list is cut mid-sentence at 45 entries.

Nothing was exercised. Every data surface is empty (history, users, tests, KB, tools, phone numbers, batches, WhatsApp, analytics shows '---'), no call or chat was started, no number imported, no CSV uploaded, no batch submitted. So conversation records, history columns, test runs, simulations, invoices, campaigns and the Spotlight page were never seen.

Workspace sidebar: Home, Architect, Triage; Agents (+ Create agent); Configure (Knowledge Base, Tools, Integrations, Voices); Monitor (Conversations, Users, Tests); Deploy (Channels, Phone Numbers, WhatsApp, Outbound); Settings; Developers; Upgrade; an 'Invite team members' card; a 'Search & create' box (Cmd K). The sidebar can collapse to an icon-only rail with no labels.

Agent-level sidebar: Overview (Spotlight, Dashboards, Architect [Alpha], Triage); Configure (Agent, Procedures, Workflow, Version Control, Knowledge Base, Analysis, Tools, Guardrails, Settings); Monitor (Conversations, Tests, Users); Deploy (Channels, Outbound); Developers. Agent and branch (Main) are switched at the top of the sidebar. The label 'Outbound' opens a page titled 'Batch Calling'.

Maturity is labelled in the UI: Alpha on Architect (sidebar), the KB Memory tab, per-agent Alerting, 'Transcribe user speech on disabled interruptions' and five channels (Intercom, Slack, Freshdesk, Telegram, Custom Channel); Beta on 'Create with Architect'; 'Now GA' on Realtime voice mode; 'New' and 'Improved' badges on promos. The Widget channel row is dimmed with no reason shown.

The 'New agent' chooser offers five paths: Create with Architect (Beta, focused first), Browse Templates, Personal Assistant, Business Agent (Improved), Blank Agent. The blank path has one required field (Agent Name, 50 characters, placeholder '[Tag] Agent name') and a 'Chat only' checkbox, then 'Create Agent'. Three pagination dots appear under the chooser with no visible way to reach more.

After login the landing view is a template gallery, not an empty agent list: at least 45 templates with a live node-graph preview and 'Use template' one click away. Cards show only a one-line description and 'N integrations / N tools / ElevenLabs' badges, with no price, voice or language. The list is US-shaped (a 'Collections' template says FDCPA compliant, a benefits line names 401k, HVAC home services) and no template is India-specific; outbound templates exist (Renewal & Expansion, Accounts Receivable, Outbound Dialer with Voicemail Handling, Outbound Sales Representative, Appointment Reminder).

A freshly created agent already runs on defaults with no further required field: system prompt 'You are a helpful assistant.', first message 'Hello! How can I help you today?', voice Eric - Smooth, Trustworthy, language English, LLM DeepSeek Flash 4.1, TTS V4 Turbo, ASR Scribe v2 Realtime. Publish is greyed while the page is a draft, with no explanation.

Steps to a first browser test: sign-in (about 15 s, no OTP, per Instinct), New agent, Blank Agent, type a name, Create Agent, then type or speak in the docked panel on the right: 4 clicks and 1 required field before a test chat. A first phone call is not reachable from the dashboard alone: it needs an imported number (7 Exotel fields, or Twilio or SIP credentials) and an agent-to-number link that was never seen.

The Agent tab holds: system prompt editor (wand button, expand, 'Type {{ to add variables', timezone chip), first message with an 'Interruptible' toggle and a 'Disclosure Requirements' link, Voice mode (Realtime | Custom), Voices (primary plus additional), Language (default plus additional), LLM, Agent behavior (personality and channel-specific reply behaviour). A test panel (Inline | Widget, Mock tools, debug, expand) stays docked on every agent page.

The Settings page has three tabs (Advanced, Security, Architect). Advanced sections in order: Multimodal input, Automatic Speech Recognition, Conversational behavior, LLM cascade timeout, Client events, Alerting (Alpha), Privacy. Security sections: Authentication, Allowlist, Overrides (17 toggles), Conversation Initiation Client Data Webhook, Post-call Webhook, Limits (daily call limit, concurrent limit, bursting, queuing, max queue wait, custom hold audio). Every control has a one- or two-sentence description.

The primary-LLM drawer lists 45 models plus a Custom LLM in five groups: Hosted by ElevenLabs (5), Anthropic (11), Google (8), OpenAI (21), Custom. It has search only (no sort or filter), a 'Detailed costs' button, and two one-line descriptions (DeepSeek Flash 4.1, GLM 5.2). Some rows (Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5) carry an expand chevron.

Each LLM row shows a latency figure and an approximate cost per minute and per message. Per-minute cost runs from about $0.0004 (GPT-5 Nano) to $0.0750 (GPT-6 Astra), about 190x; the default DeepSeek Flash 4.1 shows 230 ms to 1.85 s and about $0.0078 per minute. Latency is a range on most rows and a single '~' value on eight rows, so rows are not like-for-like, and no percentile, region or condition is stated on the list.

At the default model the vendor-displayed platform fee ($0.08/min) plus LLM ($0.0078/min) is about $0.0878, or about INR 8.3 at FX 95, before telephony and the 5% silence rate. Across the list the displayed LLM + platform total spans $0.0804 to $0.155 (INR 7.6 to 14.7); even the dearest listed LLM is below the platform fee. In burst ($0.16) the default is about INR 15.9.

The dashboard's per-minute LLM costs are lower than the free calculator we read through the API on 2026-10-20 at a similar implied 5.2 to 5.3 messages per minute: DeepSeek Flash 4.1 $0.0078 vs $0.0130, Claude Sonnet 4.5 $0.0248 vs $0.0558, GPT-4o $0.0180 vs $0.0415 (1.7x to 2.3x). Same message rate, lower per-message price, so the dashboard probably assumes a smaller prompt. The assumption is not stated on the list and was not opened (the 'Detailed costs' panel was not captured).

The dashboard shows 45 of the 111 values the API enum listed on 2026-10-20 (43 of those 111 were deprecated or in warning), so the picker is a curated subset, but deprecation alone does not account for the gap of 66. No Indian or Indic-tuned LLM provider appears in any group.

The LLM drawer also exposes: Backup LLM configuration (Default | Custom | Disabled), Temperature (More deterministic to More expressive, plus 'Don't send temperature'), Reasoning Effort (Default, High, Max, further options not captured), Reasoning summary, Limit token usage (-1 = no limit), Soft timeout (shown as Disabled), Parallel tool calling. Which option is selected for most of these is not in the text.

Voice is set in an 'Agent voice' drawer: a single collapsed voice row, TTS model family 'V4 Turbo' with a 'Fastest' badge, Expressive mode ON, ten suggested audio-tag chips (Empathetically, Confidently, Warmly, Excitedly, Patiently, Enthusiastically, Seriously, Chuckles, Laughing, Sighs) plus an Add button, and Stability (about 50%) and Similarity (about 74%) sliders with end labels only and no numeric readout. The 'Fastest' badge is the only speed or quality cue; no latency, credit or price is shown beside the model.

Voice mode is a two-way switch, Realtime | Custom, with Custom active and a 'Now GA' badge. A dismissable card says 'Try Realtime voice mode - Faster, simpler voice agents'. Nothing says what changes (the speech-to-speech path versus the ASR-LLM-TTS cascade), what it costs or which languages it supports, and it was not switched.

The voice library (Explore | My Voices) has a Language dropdown, seven category chips, use-case cards (Customer Support, Sales, Coach, Personal Assistants), an 'Iconic Voices' carousel of licensed celebrity or character voices and per-voice rows with a '+N' extra-language count and two icon-only stats. Every visible voice is English (US, UK or Australian); no Indic voice appears in the captured rows and the Language filter was not opened, so the Indic voice count is unknown. Voices carry no price.

The default-language drawer lists 88 languages under the default filter 'Compatible with agent config'; 'All languages' was not captured. South Asian entries: Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu (14). There is no Hinglish or Hindi-English row. No row shows quality tier, latency or price. English carries a US flag.

The word 'Hinglish' appears nowhere on the captured pages except the name of a second agent in the workspace sidebar ('[TEARDOWN] Synthetic Hinglish renewal agent', ours). The API-only hinglish_mode flag found on 2026-10-20 has no visible control on the captured Agent, Settings or Analysis pages; the Agent behavior drawer, which could hold it, was not opened.

Conversational behaviour controls on Settings: Eagerness (Normal), Spelling patience (Auto), Interruption ignore terms, Speculative turn, Re-transcribe audio on turn timeout, Transcribe user speech on disabled interruptions (Alpha), Turn model (Turn V3), Take turn after silence (seconds, -1 = wait indefinitely), End conversation after silence (Disabled), Max conversation duration (seconds), LLM cascade timeout (seconds). Only Normal, Auto, Turn V3 and Disabled show a value in the text; the rest need the 2026-10-20 API read-back of this same agent.

API read-back of this same dashboard-created agent (2026-10-20): turn_timeout 7.0 s, silence_end_call_timeout -1 (never), turn_eagerness normal, speculative_turn true, retranscribe_on_turn_timeout false, turn_model turn_v3, interruption_ignore_terms empty, soft timeout -1 (off), cascade timeout 4.0 s, max duration 600 s, VAD background-voice filter false. The dashboard values that are visible (Normal, Turn V3, Disabled, Auto) match.

Turn-taking is exposed as an eagerness enum plus a model choice and a silence timeout in seconds, not as millisecond endpointing or reply-delay constants. A banner says the ASR setting is locked because 'Turn V3 requires Scribe v2 Realtime', so the turn model and the ASR are one coupled choice.

Contrast with Bolna's code (earlier lanes): Bolna holds a reply about 1.4 s (500 ms endpointing plus a 900 ms linear delay) and drops short replies spoken while the agent talks. ElevenLabs exposes no equivalent constants, so a buyer cannot see or tune where its floor sits; the one lever visible for short back-channel words ('haan', 'hmm') is the Interruption ignore terms list, whose default for this English agent is empty. Whether that default explains the 4 of 16 'Are you still there?' answers to 'haan'/'hmm' measured on 2026-10-17 is untested.

The help text for Interruption ignore terms gives English examples ('gotcha', 'understood', 'yeah') and says turning it on 'seeds safe defaults for the agent's languages'. Whether a Hindi preset exists and what it contains was not shown.

By default the agent cannot end a call or detect voicemail or play keypad tones: all nine system tools (End conversation, Detect language, Skip turn, Update state, Transfer to agent, Transfer to number, Play keypad touch tone, Voicemail detection, Flag issue for review) are OFF ('0 active tools'). Enable DTMF input is OFF and says only out-of-band tones through Telephony, Twilio or Genesys are supported. Filter background speech is OFF. End-conversation-after-silence is Disabled, so with no end-call tool the only built-in stop is the max duration (600 s per the read-back).

Security > Limits: daily call limit, concurrent call limit ('Using subscription limit'), Enable bursting ('exceed the workspace subscription concurrency limit by up to 3 times, with excess calls charged at double the normal rate'), Enable call queuing, Max queue wait time, Custom hold audio (default hold tone, MP3 or WAV up to 40 MB, max 3 min). The toggle states are not in the text; the read-back of this agent has bursting_enabled true, queue enabled with a 180 s wait and a daily limit of 100,000.

The noisy-environment detection and its spoken message that the API read-back carries have no control in the captured Settings page; the page offers only 'Filter background speech' for noise. The first message in the default agent has no AI disclosure, though a 'Disclosure Requirements' link sits beside the first-message label.

Workspace Tools has three creation tiles (webhook, client, Integration tool) and filters Type, Creator, Agent. The per-agent Tools page has Tools | MCP tabs, 'Add tool', and the nine system tools. The Integrations page is an MCP-server table (empty) over a library of four cards: Cursor, HubSpot, ServiceNow, Zendesk. No India-relevant integration (CRM, payments, WhatsApp BSP, telephony) is in the library.

Workspace KB: five equal-weight tiles (Add URL, Add Files, Create Text, Create Folder, Sync Documents) and a pill 'RAG Storage: 0 B / 1.0 MB' on the Free plan. Agent KB has tabs Sources, Memory (Alpha) and Retrieval, a 'Test retrieval' button and a table (Name, Created by, Last updated). The Memory tab shows cross-call memory has a dashboard surface, but its contents and whether it is usable on Free were not seen.

Workflow is a node canvas, empty on a new agent (only a Start node), with a 10-icon toolbar (undo, redo, zoom, fit, layers, copy, Templates with a green dot, search, chart), a Global settings panel with 'Prevent infinite loops' (OFF) and a banner 'To enable a workflow, connect the start node to an entry node'. Template workflows show named nodes with opening-line prompts, conditional edges in English ('The caller has a technical issue...') and tool badges. Procedures is a separate free-form feature ('Teach your agent to handle a specific task in natural language'), empty, with a 'New procedure' dropdown.

Test surfaces: a docked Inline | Widget panel with Mock tools, a full-screen Preview (History, Debugger, Voice settings, Vars, Mock tools, Mute, chat input, Eleven v4 promo banner), a per-agent Tests page (Attached Tests | Past Test Runs, 'Add test', 'Learn how'), a 'Testing' tab on Dashboards and a 'Test call' button in the batch form. All empty; the Architect checklist names 'Simulation tests covering scenarios' as a go-live item but no simulation UI was captured.
A red circular alert-style button sits on the orb on every preview and test panel (idle, draft, empty), with no label or tooltip. It may be an error or a start control; the pixels do not say.

Quality and ops surfaces: Analysis tab (default analysis model Gemini 2.5 Flash, Topic discovery ON, Sentiment analysis ON with an 'Acknowledge' notice that text only is analysed, Analysis Language Auto, Auto-translate transcript OFF, Source Attribution ON, Evaluation criteria 0, Data collection 0); Triage (Pending, In progress, Resolved, Cancelled; columns Agent, Creator, Assignee, Created); a 'Flag issue for review' system tool; per-agent Alerting (Alpha, notifications and thresholds unconfigured); Dashboards with 12 tabs and a Spotlight button.

Architect (Alpha) is the LLM build-and-fix assistant: a prompt box ('build a tool, fix a behavior, or investigate an alert; @ to reference, / for commands'), hold-to-talk voice input, seven shortcut tiles, Home and Inbox tabs, chat history and Customization. A pill says it is 'free to use during the alpha, through October 2026' with no post-alpha price. Below the fold is a 'Deployment checklist, 0 of 10 ready before going live' (agents.md, user.md, guardrails, KB auto-sync, procedures, simulation tests, custom data, eval criteria, live on a channel, flags issues) and a Triage panel.

Version Control has Branches | Proposals | Contributors tabs, Graph, Traffic split and Create branch buttons. The one branch, Main, shows 100% traffic with a green 'Live' badge, 0 conversations in 7 days and the creator team@vyakti.ai; the table scrolls sideways so at least one column is hidden. The agent-level sidebar and the Preview toolbar both carry a branch selector.

Phone Numbers has one acquisition path, Import number, with three sources: From Twilio, From SIP Trunk, From Exotel. There is no buy-a-number option and no country, price or KYC step. The Exotel panel asks for 7 inputs: Label (0/50), phone number (country code defaults to +91), Account SID, API Key, API Token (masked), Region, Voicebot Applet ID. Region defaults to 'Singapore (api.exotel.com)'; 'Mumbai (api.in.exotel.com)' is the other option in the text.

Channels lists 10 rows: Telephony, WhatsApp (calls and messaging via WhatsApp Business), Widget (dimmed), Zendesk, Genesys, Intercom, Slack, Freshdesk, Telegram, Custom Channel, with a 'Request a channel' button. The WhatsApp page is a separate empty accounts list with 'Import account'. No page mentions TRAI, DLT, KYC, 140/160 series or an Indian carrier other than the Exotel option.

Outbound is a single-page 'Create a batch call' form, not a wizard. A header menu first asks the channel (Telephony | WhatsApp). The form has 7 inputs: Batch name ('Untitled Batch'), Phone Number (disabled: 'Please add a phone number to start batch calling'), Ringing timeout (60 s), Concurrency limit (optional, 'Auto'), Select Agent, Recipients (CSV or XLS, max 25.0 MB; required column phone_number; optional prompt, first_message, voice_id, language; any other column becomes a dynamic variable), Timing (Send immediately | Schedule for later). The footer has 'Test call' and 'Submit a Batch Call', both disabled, with no reason given.

Scheduling adds exactly two fields: a start date-time (default 'Today, 12:44 AM') and a timezone (default Asia/Calcutta). No per-recipient calling window, daily hours, retry rule, do-not-call or consent control, price estimate or compliance field is on the form or the batch list. No campaign, lead or suppression page exists in the self-serve sidebar.

Dashboards has 12 tabs (General, Evaluation, Data Collection, Workflow, Audio, Queue, Tools, LLMs, Topics, Knowledge Base, Advanced, Testing), a toolbar (Create view, date range 'Last 7 days UTC+5:30', Granularity Hourly, Agent chip, Branch, Group by, Stacked view), six metric tabs (Number of conversations, Average duration, Total cost, Average cost, Total LLM cost, Average LLM cost) and cards for Overall Success Rate, Average CSAT, Agent Response Time and Total Conversation Duration. Everything shows '---'; the CSAT card says feedback must be enabled in the widget. History has search, an Agent chip, Filters and 'Customize table'; Users searches by user ID only.

The ElevenAgents subscription tab (USD only) shows: Free $0, 15 minutes, 4 concurrent, 10,000 credits; Starter $6 (first month $1) 75 min, 6 concurrent; Creator $22 (first month $11) 275 min, 10; Pro $99, 1,238 min, 20; Scale $299, 3,738 min, 30 concurrent, 3 workspace seats; Business $990, 12,375 min, 40, 10 seats, 10 voice clones; Enterprise custom (DPA/SLA, HIPAA BAA, custom SSO). Calls $0.08/min on every plan, text $0.0030/message, burst $0.16/min, additional minutes $0.08/min; LLM and telephony rows read 'Based on usage and varies by model'.

Plan price divided by included minutes is $0.0800 on Starter, Creator and Business ($6/75, $22/275, $990/12,375) and $0.0800 to within $0.0001 on Pro and Scale, equal to the pay-as-you-go rate. So the 'minutes included' are prepaid platform fee, not a volume discount; tiers buy concurrency, seats and features. The odd minute counts (1,238, 3,738, 12,375) are the price over $0.08.

No INR price, UPI option or India tax line is visible on the subscription tab; the FAQ list includes 'How is tax handled for Alabama customers?'. The earlier claim of INR and UPI checkout is therefore not seen in the dashboard captures (the Billing portal behind the 'Billing' button was not opened). The Telephony-provider row is captioned 'Based on usage and varies by model', a copy error for a carrier fee.

Workspace Settings (General, Architect tabs) has four empty slots: Conversation Initiation Client Data Webhook, Workspace Secrets, Auth Connections, Post-Call Webhook. Developers has seven tabs (Overview, API Keys, Webhooks, Analytics, Request Log, Alerts, Environment variables); API Keys lists one user key with a red warning triangle and no tooltip, created Oct 20, expires Never, enabled. Team features seen: an 'Invite team members' card, a Users page of end users, seats on Scale (3) and Business (10), SSO on Enterprise; roles, audit log and invoices were not captured.

Agent Security tab: Enable authentication OFF; Allowlist empty with a red box 'Any host will be able to connect to this agent'; 17 override toggles, all OFF except 'Text only' (Agent language, First message, Workflow start node, System prompt, LLM, Voice, Additional voices, Voice speed, Voice stability, Voice similarity, Pronunciation dictionaries, Text only, Max conversation duration, ASR keywords, Tools, Knowledge base, Procedures). Privacy (Advanced tab) has Zero Retention Mode, Store Call Audio and Conversations Retention Period (Unlimited); the read-back shows audio stored and no redaction.

Contradiction: the 2026-10-20 public teardown listed defaults 'LLM gemini-2.5-flash ... speculative turn off'. A dashboard-created agent defaults to DeepSeek Flash 4.1 (screenshot) with speculative_turn true (API read-back), as the account phase already found; the OpenAPI defaults are not what the dashboard creates.

Confirmation and nuance on the hidden campaigns product: the 2026-10-20 bundle analysis found a lead-level campaigns surface. A new Free workspace shows none of it: the Outbound page is 'Batch Calling' and its create menu offers only Telephony or WhatsApp. This is consistent with the pre-registered EL-P04 expectation that a new self-serve workspace would probably not see it (at most 30%).

Only the dashboard showed: the full 45-template gallery with workflow previews; the exact Exotel import form (7 fields, Mumbai and Singapore regions); the batch form's CSV contract and its two scheduling fields; a 10-item Architect deployment checklist; 'Interruption ignore terms', 'Spelling patience' and 'Re-transcribe on timeout' as labelled controls; a coupling banner between Turn V3 and Scribe v2 Realtime; the Memory (Alpha) tab; the per-row LLM latency and cost strip; plan concurrency and seat limits.

Not decidable from the captures: what a default agent does on a live Indian-handset call (hang-up on silence, burst surcharge, back-channel handling, language hold), whether Hindi presets exist for interruption ignore terms, what the hinglish_mode flag does and where it lives, what the batch export contains, what failure reasons look like, and what Realtime mode changes. Each needs a live call or a number.
